description: A three-tap stereo delay: one delay time, pan and feedback setting for all three taps, with a per-tap offset on each, and a switch choosing how long the buffer is

params.text: Sets the delay time all three taps are offset from, as a fraction of the buffer length
Attenuverts the delay CV before it is added to the delay knob
Shifts that tap's delay away from the global time, a whole buffer length either way
Shifts that tap's delay away from the global time, a whole buffer length either way
Shifts that tap's delay away from the global time, a whole buffer length either way
Sets where all three taps are placed across the stereo field before their own offsets, hard left to hard right
Attenuverts the pan CV before it is added to the pan knob
Shifts that tap's position across the stereo field away from the global pan, the whole width either way
Shifts that tap's position across the stereo field away from the global pan, the whole width either way
Shifts that tap's position across the stereo field away from the global pan, the whole width either way
Sets how much of each tap is fed back into the buffer, 0 to 100 per cent before the per-tap offsets
Attenuverts the feedback CV before it is added to the feedback knob
Shifts that tap's feedback away from the global setting, -100 to 100 per cent
Shifts that tap's feedback away from the global setting, -100 to 100 per cent
Shifts that tap's feedback away from the global setting, -100 to 100 per cent
Sets the balance between the untreated signal and the three taps, none to all wet
Attenuverts the dry and wet CV before it is added to the mix knob
Wipes the delay buffer on each press, a slice at a time until it is empty
Cuts the input off and lets the buffer circulate on its own while it is held, so the delay becomes a loop
Picks how long the buffer is, 36, 360 or 3600ms, which is also the span both the delay knob and the tap offsets are measured against

inputs.text: The left signal into the delay; with nothing patched, the right input feeds both sides
The right signal into the delay; with nothing patched, the left input feeds both sides
Changes the global delay time, added to the delay knob through its attenuverter at one thousandth of the buffer length per volt scaled against 36ms
Changes the global pan, added to the pan knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the full width
Changes the global feedback, scaled by a hundredth and added to the feedback knob through its attenuverter
Changes the dry and wet balance, scaled by a hundredth and added to the mix knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to none through all wet
Any voltage above 0V wipes the delay buffer, added to the clear button rather than edge-detected
Any voltage above 0V holds the buffer circulating and cuts the input off, added to the hold button rather than edge-detected

outputs.text: The left side of the delayed and mixed signal
The right side of the delayed and mixed signal

notes: the delay knob and the three tap offsets are read as fractions of the buffer length, so changing the BUFFER SIZE switch changes every delay time at once
menu: Delay Time: 36 ms, 360 ms, 3600 ms — sets the buffer length, but the BUFFER SIZE switch on the panel overwrites it on the very next audio sample, so the choice made here does not hold
